18. Moreouet Enoch begat Irad, and Irad begat Mauiael, and Mauiael the ling oulie
begat Mathuſael, and Mathuſael begat Lamech. 19. Who tooke (d) two
wiues, the name of the one was Ada, and the namne of the other Sella.
20. And Ada brought forth Iabel, who was the tather ot them that
dwel in tents, and ot heardſmen. 21. And his brothers name was Iubal:
he was the father of them that ſing on harp & organes. 22. Sella alſo
brought torth Tubalcain, who was a hammerer anc worket in al
worke ot braſſe and iron. And the ſiſter of Tubalcain was Noema.
23. Aud Lamech ſaid to his wiues Ada and Sella : Heare my voice ve beare armes
wiues of Lamech, harken to my talke: for I haue ſlaine a man to the
woundins ot my ſelte, and a ſtripeling to mine owne drie blow bru-
fing. 24. Seauen- told vengeanec ſhal be taken ot Cain: but of Lamech
Adam alſo knew his wite againe: and ſhe brought totth a ſonne,
& called his name Seth, ſaving: God hath giuen me other ſeed tor Abel,
whom Cain flew. 26. But to Seth alto was bornea ſonne whom he cal-
led Enos, this man ‖ began to inuocate the name ot our Lord.
.OFered gufes.) Either God himſelfe taught Adam, and he his chil dren, or
vls they knew by inſtinct of nature, that Sacrifice muſt be offered to God, to
acknowledge thereby his ſupreme dominion ouer man, and mans due fubiection
to hit diuine Maieſtit. And that not only in internal affection, which (as S.
Auguſtin, and al Catholike Doctours teach) is principally required , but alſo
in external things, becauſe we conſiſt of bodie, and not only of foule, and haue,
by Cods goudpes, the vſe of corporal things. As here we ſee example in the law
of nature: and the ſame was ordained by written precept in the law of Movſes:
the Prophets alſo toretold, that external Sacrifice ſhould be oftered in the law
of grace and new Teſtament , to wit , the ſame which Chriſt inſtituted , and left
in his Church, to continue to the end of the world. Moreouer this hoinage of
oftering Sacrifice is ſo peculiar to God only, that albeit manie other exteriour
rites aud ſctuices are vſed both to God & men, as to be bare-head, to bow, to
kneel, & the like before thein euher ogreat humilitie ( ſaith S Auguſtin) to of
peſt iferous ſlatterie, to ſuch as are hominer toiendi, venerandi, ſ autem eiaum
additur, & adorandi: men to be wor: hippe d, yeuereuced, aud if much be g: uen them , adored;
(tor this terme ot adoring is alfo applied to men in holie Scriptures, Gen. 23.v. 7. 17.
v.29) yet Sacrifice is due to God only, and to no creature how excellent ſo
euer. In fo much ( ſaith the ſame Doctour that as al nations found it neceſfaric
to offer Sacrifice, ſo none durſt ſacrifice to anie, niſi ei ouem Deum aut ſtiuit, aut
